base_and_residual.base: the corresponding analysis GlucoBench linear regression, in_len=24 (target lags at 5-minute spacing, offsets -115 .. 0), min-max scaler and OLS fitted on the training rows of each protocol; coefficients frozen
base_and_residual.form: fixed-baseline residual augmentation: r = y - y_hat_base; ridge-penalised factor block f(x) fitted on r; prediction y_hat_base + f(x). Not equivalent to a joint ARX fit; joint ARX is not executed (T18 none).
base_and_residual.factor_block_preprocessing: imputation and standardization fitted on the training rows only (as in the corresponding analysis)

availability_rules.glucose_derived_candidates: inferred native-reading anchors only (anchor_rule); no interpolated minute after the newest anchor; the base's 24 interpolated lags are unchanged and are tested by E8
availability_rules.MET: only with a lag of at least 10 minutes (REC 3.4 primitives); the REC activity grid lists heart rate and activity calories only, so no MET candidate is enumerated. The existing A-group features of M include MET windows ending at t (REC 2.6 method specification: possible slight look-ahead); E1 reports them as locked.
availability_rules.HbA1c: percent (original paper p.2, Table 2; the dictionary label mmol/mol is a dictionary error)

baseline_metabolic_covariates.BMI: kg/m2; enrollment measurement; main interaction family (confirm at method specification)
baseline_metabolic_covariates.laboratory_values: fasting glucose [mg/dL], fasting insulin [uU/mL, dictionary mcU/mL], HbA1c [percent], HOMA-IR = glucose x insulin / 405; availability at the prediction time not provable: conditional family only (pending_decisions.Q7_baseline_covariates)

availability_rules.M_composition: 50 existing features = 47 window-level A/D primary features (activity_diet_feature_registry, variant primary) + 3 core B features (age, gender, BMI)
availability_rules.meal_events: logged meal row time (about the pre-meal photo time) as the event time; nutrients known at that time for the designed breakfast and lunch; the 30-minute delayed version is generated for E9

anchor_rule.name: inferred native-reading anchors (statistical inference from the second difference; the raw CSV and the data dictionary carry no native-reading flag)
anchor_rule.parameter_status: formally retained by the user (min_kinks, support_kinks, min_phase_share, max_stale_minutes); n_anchors 8 for the native-state family, 9 for the E8-a rebuild

levels.confirmed: reliable phase grid and the kink at the second-newest anchor is present
levels.grid: reliable phase grid and that kink is absent (collinear neighbors; a reading missing from the schedule is indistinguishable)
levels.uncertain: fewer than min_kinks supporting kinks, phase not consistent, newest supporting kink older than max_stale_minutes, or fewer than two anchors

anchor_rule.causal_rule: prefix_causal only: the phase at t uses kinks at or before t - 15 minutes (a kink reads the following minute, which already points at the next reading); the features at t use only values on anchors at or before t

model_facing_fields.missing_indicator: anchor_missing = level is uncertain, or fewer than the 5 anchors an operator needs are available
model_facing_fields.derived_features: every native-state feature is a function of the anchor fields only, computed with row-independent arithmetic (a batched matrix product changed the last bits between a full run and a truncated run in the analysis closing check) and set to NaN where anchor_missing
model_facing_fields.gate: analysis repeats the truncation and perturbation tests on the final model-facing columns before any use

conservative_rule_draft: only anchors on a reliable phase grid are used
native-reading features of `uncertain` windows are NaN plus a missing indicator, never interpolated values (method specification)
E8 pairs windows with reliable anchors only and reports the excluded share
anchors are always called inferred native-reading anchors
anchor_rule.wording: the anchors are inferred native-reading anchors, never described as directly observed native readings

candidate_families.source_primitives: meal events (carbs, protein, fat, fiber, calories) by meal type; hr and activity_calories with coverage mask; BMI; native-reading glucose state; every operator declares its earliest source time and a single function checks max_source_offset <= 0

meal_x_baseline_state.tau_k: (tau, k) pair of carbs for the same meal type (joint selection, method specification)

activity_kernels.activity_x_meal_kernel: exp_decay(activity, tau) x conv_gamma(carbs) at tau*

candidate_families.planned_size_note: sizes assume tau_per_k is not chosen; with tau_per_k the main interaction family doubles
candidate_families.counts_check: main 206 = 160 absorption + 12 BMI/native-state interactions + 6 ratios + 24 activity + 4 native state; conditional lab family +12; consistent with joint (tau, k) and with Q7 (verified)

tau_star_rule.rule: for each nutrient x meal type the (tau, k) pair with the largest |mean subject-level Spearman IC| (method specification: abs(mean IC), joint (tau, k)); the signed mean IC and the same-sign share are reported

screening.ic: subject-level Spearman IC against r, windows downsampled to a 15-minute step, then mean IC and same-sign share across subjects (A: 45, B: 27)

keep_per_family.ranking: |mean IC| (method specification), computed on the protocol's own training data

screening.redundancy_filter: drop a candidate with |rho| > 0.9 against a base feature or an already kept factor
screening.p_values_and_fdr: descriptive only (one-sample t / Wilcoxon, BY correction); never an inclusion threshold; candidates are not called statistically significant

selection.method: forward selection, each step adds the factor with the largest drop in validation subject-equal RMSE
selection.stopping: smallest set within one standard error of the best validation curve; the full curve is recorded

evaluation.primary_metric: subject-equal RMSE (pooled-window metrics also reported); main comparison: paired subject-equal delta RMSE against the GlucoBench LR base
evaluation.min_windows_rule_note: REC 4.3: applies to subject-equal averages of evaluation subsets; also reported without the rule
evaluation.multiplicity: Holm over the 4 main contrasts per protocol

E1.definition: existing 50 features M (47 A/D + 3 core B) as a residual block on the fixed base; contrasts follow ablation_matrix.csv
E1.loco: feature-level drop-one / add-one validation delta RMSE, subject-paired, validation only

openfe.train_index_val_index: explicit (A: last 25% of each training period as internal validation; B: 18/9 subject-grouped split of the 27 training subjects)
openfe.init_scores: OOF per oof_specification; the internal split uses the separate_openfe_init_scores rule
openfe.settings_source: library defaults of openfe 0.0.12 except feature_boosting (default False; True is required for init_scores)
openfe.inputs: M, non-glucose primitives, baseline metabolic covariates allowed by Q7, native-reading state; no interpolated glucose lags, no subject column
openfe.operators_excluded: all GroupByThen*, Combine*, freq (they use statistics across rows)
openfe.transform_application: the selected formulas are applied by project code with training-set statistics only

protocol_A.blocks: 5 equal-duration time blocks inside each subject's training period [start_time, protocol_a_train_end_time] (edges in block_edges)
protocol_A.cross_fitting: non-forward: block b is predicted by a base fitted on the retained training windows of the other blocks; fits pooled over the protocol's training windows
protocol_A.support_rule: a window belongs to a block only if its whole support [history_start_time, target_time] lies in it; the others are dropped (5,117 of 79,300 windows, 6.45%, accepted by the user); the dropped windows are in no fit and have no OOF residual
protocol_A.effect: factor-block training rows, IC screening and OpenFE only (74,183 rows); the evaluation windows are unchanged

protocol_B.folds: GroupKFold(n_splits=5), deterministic, no shuffle, groups = the 27 training subjects; validation and test subjects take no part in any fold fit
protocol_B.reproduction: membership computed from the admitted training keys of fold_assignments (window counts per subject balance the folds); to be saved with the analysis base residuals

oof_specification.all_residuals: every training window with a compliant OOF rule gets its OOF residual; validation and test rows use the base fitted on the full training split; scalers, imputers, standardizers and any other fitted preprocessing are fitted inside each fold's training part only

protocol_A.internal_split: per subject the first 75% of the training period is internal-train (whole support before the 75% cut) and the rest internal-validation (whole support after the cut); windows crossing the cut are dropped from both (REC 4.1 internal validation = last 25%)
protocol_A.internal_train_init_scores: OOF inside the internal-train period: 5 equal-duration blocks of that period, non-forward, crossing windows dropped
protocol_A.internal_validation_init_scores: base fitted on all internal-train windows only

protocol_B.internal_split: 18 internal-train / 9 internal-validation subjects among the 27 training subjects (REC 3.6 example); membership: internal_membership
protocol_B.internal_train_init_scores: GroupKFold(5) OOF inside the 18 subjects, deterministic
protocol_B.internal_validation_init_scores: base fitted on the 18 internal-train subjects only

internal_membership.rule: the 27 Protocol-B training subject ids are sorted; permutation = numpy.random.default_rng(42).permutation(sorted ids); the first 18 are internal-train, the last 9 internal-validation; Protocol-B validation and test subjects are never used

openfe_init_scores.rule: no internal-validation label, lag, residual or fold fit reaches the internal-train data through the base, the residual target, the init_scores, the preprocessing parameters or the folds; the final O_k factor block is trained on the main OOF residuals
openfe_init_scores.consequence: A: 5,157 of the 58,895 internal-train windows (8.8%) have no init_score because of the block edges, in addition to 1,290 windows crossing the 75% cut

primary_endpoint: Paired subject-equal RMSE change relative to fixed GlucoBench predictions
